title: Chapter 20 — Specialty Categories
intro: Wine storage, beverage centres, ice makers, outdoor kitchens, and the categories that complete the luxury home.

sections.title: Wine Storage
sections.content:
Wine storage is a lifestyle product that sells on emotion and justifies on preservation. The customer who invests in a wine unit is telling you about their entertaining style, their collection, and their home design.

Key specs: temperature zones — single zone for one type, dual zone for reds and whites at different temperatures. Capacity — measured in bottles, typically 24 to 300+ depending on unit size. UV-protected glass door. Vibration dampening — important for long-term aging. Built-in versus freestanding — built-in requires ventilation clearance.

Sub-Zero, Miele, and Liebherr lead the premium wine storage category. Know the differences: Sub-Zero's air management and temperature stability are best-in-class. Miele offers integration with their full kitchen ecosystem. Liebherr brings Swiss precision at a slightly more accessible price.

sections.title: Outdoor Kitchens
sections.content:
Outdoor kitchens are growing fast and the margins are excellent. The category includes grills (gas, charcoal, hybrid), outdoor refrigerators, ice makers, outdoor-rated dishwashers, pizza ovens, and warming drawers.

The brands: Lynx, DCS, Alfresco, and Kalamazoo at the luxury tier. Coyote, Blaze, and Broil King at mid-range. Weber and Napoleon at entry. Know the outdoor-rated distinction — indoor appliances used outdoors void the warranty.

The outdoor kitchen conversation is a design conversation. The customer is building an entertainment space. Show them the complete package: grill, fridge, ice maker, and access drawers. Package selling in outdoor is easier than any indoor category because the customer expects it.

sections.title: Beverage Centres and Ice Makers
sections.content:
Standalone ice makers and beverage centres are the easiest attach product in luxury kitchens. They fill the gap between the kitchen and the entertainment area — the bar, the butler's pantry, the game room.

Key selling points: clear ice versus cloudy ice (clear ice makers produce restaurant-quality ice that looks premium in cocktails). Production capacity — daily pounds of ice. Storage capacity. Drain versus drain-free models.

Present these as part of the kitchen design: 'Since you are doing the butler's pantry, a built-in beverage centre and clear ice maker would complete the space. Let me show you what fits your cabinetry.'
